title: Revise token lexicon and redesign elevation matrix for consistent surfaces
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Goal: replace the current ad-hoc token set with a compact, semantically named lexicon and a new elevation matrix that maps shadows and radii to clear interaction states. Scope: color ramps (primary/neutral/semantic), a 5-step typographic scale tuned for densities across consoles and embedded widgets, an explicit spacing/radius scale, and a leveled elevation system (ambient/overlay/depth). Why: current tokens cause duplication across components, inconsistent shadows across surfaces, and unclear mapping for dark-mode variants. Outcomes: fewer tokens, deterministic derivation rules (utility tokens generated from primitives), and an automated migration guide for component owners.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Color ramps defined with WCAG AA contrast for normal text against background at small sizes; 2) Typographic scale documented with token names and use-cases for H1..body/caption; 3) Spacing and radius scales exported as CSS variables and tokens for all platforms; 4) Elevation matrix provides shadow recipes for 4 levels and dark-mode inversions; 5) Migration guide and codemods available; 6) Figma library updated and validated by Design QA.
tasks: Inventory: audit current tokens across console/components (owners tagged)
Draft new lexicon and derivation rules (primitives vs. semantic tokens)
Define color ramps and run contrast tests against common backgrounds
Create typographic scale and update examples for data-dense tables and charts
Prototype elevation recipes and verify with accessibility and motion teams
Build codemod to rename tokens in react components
Publish Figma library and announce migration window
Coordinate with ENG for runtime token lookup and theme toggles
notes: Trade-offs discussed: keep a small set of primitives to minimize cognitive load vs. providing convenience semantic tokens for rapid product work. Agreed to keep 18 primitive color stops (9 neutrals x 2 themes) and expose 6 semantic aliases. Elevation will use 4 levels rather than 6 to reduce implementation complexity in Dedicated/Private where shadow rendering differs by runtime. We'll defer advanced adaptive radius heuristics until after rollout.

implementation_notes: Engineers should prefer semantic tokens (surface-bg, surface-border, interactive-primary) which derive from primitives via a single transformation layer. For Dedicated/Private runtimes expose both compiled CSS variables and JSON token bundles. Codemod will run in two phases: automatic renames + flagged manual fixes. Performance note: avoid creating per-component shadows at runtime; use CSS classes mapped to elevation levels.
migration_guide: Step 1: freeze new token PRs for 48 hours. Step 2: run codemod branch against your feature branch and resolve manual conflicts. Step 3: deploy Figma tokens and update component storybook knobs. Step 4: monitor console token-mismatch dashboard during rollout (link in Confluence).
risks: 1) Mid-rollout visual regressions in customer dashboards due to different shadow rasterization on on-prem browsers. 2) Breaking changes for third-party plugins referencing old token names. 3) Time required for manual fixes exceeds estimate.
mitigation_plan: Keep old tokens as deprecated aliases for one release cycle, provide clear migration scripts, and enlist design liaisons for high-risk product areas to perform visual QA.
qa_checks: Design QA checklist linked in Confluence; Frontend to run visual-diff snapshots for all affected stories in storybook.
